title: IaC mutation-safety harness for GPU infra
author: Aisha Rahman
content:
Summary

This document describes the design and implementation of the IaC mutation-safety harness we run in CI for GPU-related Terraform modules and operators. The harness focuses on detecting unsafe plan-level and state-level mutations (deletions, identity drift, expensive replacements), simulating partial failures in provider APIs, and validating tenant-facing SLOs and cost bounds before changes merge. The goal is to make Terraform/Helm operator changes for GPU infrastructure (fleet allocation, warm pools, egress NATs, attachment policies) provably safe to promote.

Why we built this

- GPU infra changes have high blast radius: instance replacement, quota exhaustion, egress changes cause tenant disruption or bill shock.
- Standard plan-only checks miss mutation classes that manifest only at apply-time or under transient cloud failure.
- We need automated, fast feedback in PRs and strong gating for production promotion.

Scope and targets

The harness currently runs against:
- core Terraform modules under eng-infra/terraform-and-iac that manage GPU pools, warm pools, and tenancy iac-adapters.
- onboarding modules that create tenant VPC subnets, NAT/egress routing, and IAM bindings.
- Kubernetes operators that reconcile node-attachment and ephemeral-sandbox leases (via Helm chart tests).

Out-of-scope (for now):
- full-scale chaos in production clusters (we run those from the chaos lab, separate program)
- stateful storage migration tests (covered by dedicated snapshot/restore pipeline)

Design principles

1) Plan-as-contract: every PR must produce a human-readable plan artifact and a machine-checkable plan digest. The digest contains resource counts, types, and a mutation fingerprint.
2) Mutation fuzzing: small, targeted modifications are injected into plan files to simulate accidental deletions, provider incompatibilities, and attribute drift. Tests assert that modules include defensive patterns (prevent_destroy, lifecycle ignore_changes where appropriate, explicit create_before_destroy for hot paths).
3) Apply-safety sandbox: destructive plans are sandbox-applied into a disposable sandbox account (ephemeral AWS sandbox) with billing caps and configured network egress fences. The apply is run with a mocked or rate-limited provider in some tests to emulate transient API failures.
4) SLO smoke checks: after sandbox apply, run a fast smoke harness that executes: 10 warmup inference requests, KV-cache health check, a tenant ingress e2e probe. Fail the PR if basic latency or error rate thresholds are breached.
5) Cost delta checks: estimate token-billing and instance-hour delta from the plan; reject or flag PRs that increase monthly cost projection by > 15% without approval.

Components

- plan-fingerprint service (internal CLI): generates JSON plan digests from terraform plan -out=FILE and normalizes provider-specific addresses.
- plan-fuzz engine (pytest plugin): applies mutation templates to the plan digest (delete resource, flip instance type, remove lifecycle block).
- sandbox deployer: builds a short-lived AWS/GCP account, allocates a constrained VPC, and runs terraform apply against it using a pre-seeded state.
- smoke harness: small python harness that performs the SLO smoke checks described above.
- CI orchestrator pipelines: Buildkite steps that run the plan, fuzz, sandbox apply, smoke checks and then post a verdict.

Test matrix (summary)

| Test name | Trigger | Fast/Slow | What it checks | Failure action |
|-----------|---------|----------|----------------|----------------|
| plan-lint | PR opened | Fast (~90s) | policy as code: no plain "destroy" without owner label; required tags present; resource limits | Block merge |
| plan-fingerprint-diff | PR update | Fast (~60s) | detects unexpected resource identity changes | Warn + require owner ack |
| mutation-delete | PR update | Medium (~6m) | inject delete of non-ephemeral resource, assert protectors present | Block merge |
| mutation-replace | PR update | Medium (~8m) | simulate instance-type change that would force replacement on 30%+ resources | Block merge + revert suggestion |
| sandbox-apply | Manual gate / promotion | Slow (30-45m) | full apply into ephemeral account and kube reconcile | Requires signoff or automated rollback |
| slo-smoke | After sandbox-apply | Slow (10m) | e2e latency/error smoke tests | Block promotion |

Guardrails and checks implemented

- plan-lint rules (examples):
  - deny: aws_instance without tags.owner or tags.team
  - deny: aws_ebs_volume with lifecycle { prevent_destroy = false } when used by gpu stateful sets
  - require: explicit create_before_destroy for node pool change where max_unavailable_tokens > 0.

- mutation templates (examples):
  - deletion-template: pick a resource matching type aws_autoscaling_group and mark delete=true in plan digest
  - replace-template: change instance_type to next-larger (p3 -> p4) in 3% to 50% of resources randomly
  - attr-drift-template: remove iam role attached to instance profile to emulate accidental detach

CI Integration (Buildkite snippets)

- PR pipeline example steps (pseudo-YAML):
  1. terraform: init & fmt & validate
  2. terraform: plan (-out=plan.tfplan) -> upload artifact
  3. plan-fingerprint -> post comment with fingerprint and checksums
  4. plan-fuzz -> run mutation-delete and mutation-replace tests (parallel)
  5. sandbox-apply (conditional): runs if PR has label "sandbox-apply" or on release branches
  6. slo-smoke -> fails pipeline if error rate > 2% or p95 latency degrades > 25% vs baseline

CLI examples

- generate fingerprint
  terraform plan -out=plan.tfplan && terraform show -json plan.tfplan > plan.json && plan-fingerprint --in plan.json --out plan.digest.json

- run a single mutation test locally
  plan-fuzz --template mutation-delete --digest plan.digest.json --run-local

Sandbox cost/time controls

We limit sandbox exposure by:
- Allocation TTL: sandboxes auto-delete in 45 minutes.
- Billing cap: we create sandboxes under a billing role that enforces a $100 cap via guardrails and billing alarms. Any sandbox approaching 80% cap sends a page to infra-oncall.
- Resource quotas: max 6 GPU instances per sandbox by default. Quotas are enforced by terraform variable overrides and identity-bound policies.

Failure modes and operator playbook

If the harness fails on a PR:
1) Plan-lint or mutation delete/replacement fails: the pipeline posts an annotated plan with resource links and required remediation actions. The author must update the module or add an explicit exception label with an owner approval.
2) Sandbox-apply fails due to provider API flakiness: the pipeline will mark the run as flaky and automatically queue two retries with exponential backoff. If all retries fail, open a failure ticket assigned to infra-iac with the sandbox logs attached.
3) SLO-smoke fails: stop promotion and create a roll/abort playbook suggestion. The release engineer must confirm if the change is safe.

Operational ownership and SLAs

- Ownership: eng-infra/iac-safety (primary) — pager for sandbox failures: oncall-infra (rotation)
- Expected SLA for harness feedback: Fast tests -> 2 minutes median; Medium tests -> 10 minutes median; Sandbox full apply -> 40 minutes median.

Oncall runbook (short)

- When sandbox apply pages on infra-oncall:
  1. Check the sandbox billing alarm and resource footprint in the sandbox account.
  2. If over cap, revoke sandbox IAM session and trigger sandbox cleanup job: scripts/cleanup-sandbox --sandbox-id $ID
  3. If API errors: capture terraform logs, escalate to cloud-provider-support if >2 distinct account errors within 30m.

Promotion policy and exceptions

- Default: PRs with any blocking failing test cannot be merged.
- Exceptions: an owner (module owner listed in CODEOWNERS) can apply an "iacsafety:approved" label with a short justification but must request a post-merge verification run (sandbox-apply) within 24 hours.

Future work and open items

- Extend fuzzing to Helm chart values and k8s operator CRD schema mutation.
- Add a lightweight emulated provider layer (wire-level) to speed up failure-mode testing without full cloud sandboxes.
- Incorporate budget-approval flow to allow controlled higher-cost sandboxes for heavy tests.

Appendix: quick reference table

| Command | Purpose | Notes |
|---------|---------|-------|
| plan-fingerprint --in plan.json --out digest.json | create normalized fingerprint | run in CI after terraform show -json |
| plan-fuzz --template mutation-delete --digest digest.json | run mutation-delete test locally | returns non-zero on detection of missing protectors |
| sandbox-create --preset gpu-small --ttl 45m | allocate ephemeral sandbox | used by sandbox-apply step |
| smoke-runner --endpoint $SANDBOX_IP | run SLO smoke checks | outputs p50/p95/error-rate |
